svg.title: LoRA: 256 times fewer, and you can see it
svg.desc: A hand-drawn whiteboard in which a densely hachured 4096 by 4096 square marked FROZEN with a padlock holds 16,777,216 parameters, while the LoRA detour beneath it is two slivers so thin they are drawn eight times thicker than true scale, meeting at a rank-eight waist and rejoining through a plus, with the arithmetic 32,768 plus 32,768 equals 65,536 and the ratio 256 circled. Below, a decaying singular-value spectrum recalls week 11, three bars compare 132.6, 21.3 and 14.2 GB against a 24 GB A10G line, and eight crossed-out full model copies are replaced by one base model with eight small adapter tabs clipped on.
svg.text: LoRA: 256 times fewer, and you can see it
both slivers drawn 8x thicker than true scale - at true scale you
could not see them at all
SVD: best rank-r fit to a matrix you HAVE.
LoRA: learn a rank-r matrix you never build.
and what it costs to hold
...which r though? sweep it, do not guess
